h: Kindness Truth and the Two Torahs

p: וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר לְיוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר.
— “After these things, Joseph was told ….”
לִכְאוֹרָה תֵּיבוֹת אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה מְיוּתָּר.
— The words “after these things” apparently seem superfluous.
גַּם לְמַעְלָה כְתִיב אָנֹכִי אֶעֱשֶׂה כִדְבָרֶךָ וַהֲוָה לוֹ לוֹמַר כֵּן אֶעֱשֶׂה וּבַתּוֹרָה אֵין אוֹת מְיוּתָּר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן כַּמָּה אוֹתִיּוֹת.
— Earlier, too, it is written, “I will do as you say,” whereas it could have said, “So I will do.” In the Torah no letter is superfluous, Heaven forbid, and certainly not several letters.

p: אָמְנָם הָעִנְיָן דִּכְתִיב וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת וְתִרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוֹס טִיבוּ וּקְשׁוֹט.
— The explanation is that it is written, “Deal with me in kindness and truth,” which Onkelos translates as tivu u-keshot.
וְהַיְינוּ טִיבוּ הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב דִּכְתִיב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק וְהוּא הַיּוּד שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ מִמִּדַּת צַדִּיק לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ הֵ״א דָּלֶ״ת הֲוַת וּמִדְאִתְעַבְּרַת בְּיוּ״ד.

— Tivu, goodness, is the light “that was good,” as it is written, “Light is sown for the righteous.” This is the yud shining from the attribute of Tzaddik to Malkhut, for, as is known, heh was originally dalet and then became pregnant with yud.

וְעַל זֶה אָמַר כִּי כֹל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ כִּי כֹל דָּא צַדִּיק וְכוּלֵי דִּי אָחִיד בִּשְׁמַיָּא וּבְאַרְעָא כְּלוֹמַר דִּיסוֹדָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאִקְרֵי כֹל אָחִיד בְּתִפְאֶרֶת דְּאִקְרֵי שָׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ דְּאִקְרֵי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א) וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.

— Of this it says, “For all that is in heaven and earth”: “For all”—this is the righteous one, and so forth, who joins heaven and earth. That is, the foundation of the world, called Kol, joins Tiferet, called heaven, to the earth, called the Congregation of Israel, as stated in the holy Zohar (I, 31a, end). This is the aspect of “Malkhut is the mouth,” the Oral Torah.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סוּכָּה מט:) תּוֹרָה לְלַמְּדָהּ זוֹ הִיא תּוֹרָה שֶׁל חֶסֶד וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁמְּלַמְּדִין לַתַּלְמִידִים.

— Thus it is said, “The Torah of kindness is upon her tongue.” This is the Oral Torah, following the Sages’ statement (Sukkah 49b), “Torah studied in order to teach it is a Torah of kindness”—the Oral Torah taught to students.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (ריט א) בַּת יְהָבָהּ לְאַבְרָהָם דִּכְתִיב וְהַשֵּׁם בֵּרַךְ אֶת אַבְרָהָם בַּכֹּל בַּת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְאַבְרָהָם וּבַכֹּל שְׁמָהּ.
— This is what the holy Zohar on this portion says (219a): He gave Abraham a daughter, as it is written, “Hashem blessed Abraham with everything.” Abraham had a daughter named Bakol.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִדַּת כֹּל שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הַיּוּ״ד לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת דְּדָלֶת הֲוֵית שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הֵ״א.
— This is the attribute of Kol, which bestows the yud upon Malkhut, formerly dalet, so that it becomes heh.
זֶהוּ מִצַּד בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם.
— This comes from Abraham’s aspect: “lovingkindness to Abraham.”

וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁבָּא מִיּוֹסֵף הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים כב:) וְסֵפֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁעֶרְכָּהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא.

— Joshua, descended from Joseph, was the root of the Oral Torah. As we have often explained concerning the statement (Nedarim 22b), “And the book of Joshua, for it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel”:

שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵיךְ הוּא נִכְלָל בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְזֶהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ דְּאִיתָא (קִידּוּשִׁין מט:) עֲשָׂרָה קַבִּין חָכְמָה יָרְדוּ לָעוֹלָם תִּשְׁעָה נָטְלָה אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.

— this is each Israelite’s portion in the Oral Torah and how it is included in the Written Torah. This is the holiness of the Land, for it is stated (Kiddushin 49b), “Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world; the Land of Israel took nine.”
וְהַיְינוּ חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְזֶהוּ תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב.
— This is the wisdom of the Oral Torah: the Torah of kindness, the light “that was good.”

h: The Union of Kindness and Truth

p: וֶאֱמֶת מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב אֱמֶת זוֹ תּוֹרָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה:) וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי.

— Truth is the attribute of our patriarch Jacob, peace be upon him: “truth to Jacob.” “Truth is Torah” (Berakhot 5b), meaning the Written Torah, as the holy Zohar states, “The Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah.”
וְיוֹסֵף הָיָה כָּלוּל מִשְּׁתֵּי הַקְּדוּשּׁוֹת וָא״ו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
— Joseph included both forms of holiness: Jacob’s vav, the Written Torah,
וְיוּ״ד שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַוָּא״ו זְעֵירָא וָא״ו הַמִּילּוּי שֶׁהִיא קְדוּשַּׁת בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— and his own yud, which is the small vav, the vav in the letter’s spelled-out form: the holiness of Malkhut, the Oral Torah.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת טִיבוּ וּקְשׁוֹט.
— Thus he said to him, “Deal with me in kindness and truth”—tivu u-keshot.
אַל נָא תִקְבְּרֵנִי בְּמִצְרָיִם שֶׁהִיא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ.
— “Please do not bury me in Egypt,” which is the nakedness of the earth.

וּנְשָׂאתַנִי מִמִּצְרַיִם הוּא כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת סוּר מֵרָע וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רב א) דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא.
— “Carry me out of Egypt” corresponds to turning away from evil, through the holiness of the Oral Torah. As stated in the Zohar (I, 202a), “Nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah.”
וְאָמַרְנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים שֶׁעִיקַּר שְׁבִירַת כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— As we have often said, the principal means of breaking the evil inclination’s power is the holiness of the Oral Torah.

p: וּקְבַרְתַּנִי בִּקְבוּרָתָם הַיְינוּ לְהַכְנִיסוֹ לִמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה דְּשָׁם הָיָה אוֹר דְּיוּקְנָא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל דְּאִיתָא (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי) תַּפּוּחַ עֲקֵבוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מַכְהֶה גַּלְגַּל חַמָּה קְלַסְתֵּר פָּנָיו עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.

— “Bury me in their burial place” means bringing him into the Cave of Machpelah, where the radiance of Adam’s image before the corruption was present. It is stated (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Acharei), “The rounded heel of Adam outshines the orb of the sun; how much more so the appearance of his face.”
וְהַיְינוּ לְמַעְלָה מִבְּחִינַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ.
— This is above the aspect of the sun.

וְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל דְּנִיטַּל זִיווֹ וְנִקְנְסָה עָלָיו מִיתָה לְתַקֵּן הַפְּגָם כֵּיוָן שֶׁסָּבַל הַמִּיתָה זָכָה לְמַדְרֵגָתוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּהַנּוֹגֵעַ לִפְרַט נַפְשׁוֹ אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן עֲדַיִין הַפְּגָם מִכָּל הָעוֹלָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר) וְכֵן זָכָה גַּם יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּשֶׁהִכְנִיסוֹ יוֹסֵף לִמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה.

— After the corruption, his radiance was taken away and death was decreed upon him to rectify the blemish. Once he endured death, he regained his original level as regards his individual soul, although the blemish had not yet been rectified throughout the world (as explained elsewhere). Our patriarch Jacob, peace be upon him, likewise attained this when Joseph brought him into the Cave of Machpelah.

וְהִנֵּה כָּל עֵסֶק יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְהוֹצִיא הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְהָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא מַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְאָז יוּכַל הוּא לִקְנוֹת מַעֲלָתוֹ וּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ.

— Jacob’s entire undertaking in this world was to bring forth the Congregation of Israel, so that they would attain the “great wealth,” the giving of the Torah; then he could acquire his own exalted station and level.
וְזֶה שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת.
— This is alluded to in “Deal with me in kindness and truth.”
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּעִיקַּר הַהַשְׁפָּעָה יוּ״ד לִבְחִינַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ שֵׁם שַׁדַּי.

— As is known, the principal bestowal of yud upon the Congregation of Israel comes through Joseph’s aspect. He is the vehicle for the attribute of “the righteous one, foundation of the world,” corresponding to the Name Shaddai.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי עִם דָּלֶ״ת יוּ״ד שֶׁתּוּכַל הַדָּלֶ״ת לְאִתְעַבְּרָא בְּיוּ״ד חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהֵם כְּנֶגֶד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ.

— Thus he said, “Deal with me”—imadi, read as im, “with,” dalet and yud—so that the dalet can become pregnant with yud: kindness and truth, the Oral Torah and the Written Torah, which, as is known, correspond to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah.
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן תּוּכַל לְהוֹצִיאֵנִי מִמִּצְרַיִם וּלְהַכְנִיסֵנִי לִמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה לִקְנוֹת מַעֲלָתִי.
— Through this you will be able to bring me out of Egypt and into the Cave of Machpelah, to acquire my exalted station.
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יוּכְרַח לָבֹא עוֹד לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְהוֹצִיא הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל.
— Otherwise, Heaven forbid, he would have to return again to this world to bring forth the great wealth.

p: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וַיֹּאמֶר אָנֹכִי עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (רלד ב) אֲמִירָה בַּחֲשַׁאי כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר וְאָמַרְתָּ בִּלְבָבְךָ וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנו ב) אָנֹכִי בֵּיהּ כָּ״ף כֶּתֶר וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי) כְּשֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּיבּוּר אָנֹכִי נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם.

— Thus it is said, “He said, I”—Anokhi. As the holy Zohar on this portion explains (234b), saying is inward and quiet, as in “You shall say in your heart.” It is also stated (Zohar III, 256b) that Anokhi contains kaf, Keter. This accords with the statement (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, section Yishakeni): when Israel heard the utterance Anokhi, Torah study was fixed in their hearts.
וְכֵן מְרַמֵּז כָּאן וַיֹּאמֶר אָנֹכִי שֶׁהִכְנִיס בְּלִבּוֹ מַדְרֵגַת וּבְחִינַת אָנֹכִי.
— Likewise, “He said, Anokhi” here alludes to his bringing the level and aspect of Anokhi into his heart.
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן אֶעֱשֶׂה כִדְבָרֶךָ שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמַר וְעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— Through this, “I will do as you say”—what he had requested in “Deal with me in kindness and truth”: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה
— Thus it is said, “After these things”:
הַדְּבָרִים הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לח) אֵין דְּבָרִים אֶלָּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי
— “things,” devarim, means words of Torah, as the Sages said (Shemot Rabbah, chapter 38), “Things means words of Torah,” and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ דָּבָר סְתָם דִּיבּוּר הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
— Thus davar, speech without qualification, means words of Torah;
יוּ״ד מֵ״ם מְרַמֵּז שֶׁהַיּוּד הַהוֹפָעָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת נַעֲשֶׂה מֵ״ם סְתוּמָה
— the ending yud-mem alludes to the yud, the illumination bestowed upon Malkhut, becoming a closed mem,

— Thus “these things” indicates that the aspect of kindness and truth, tivu u-keshot, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah, was engraved in his heart.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 234b: ““He said”—what is meant by “he said”? We have explained it, as in “You will say in your heart”: speech in a whisper. “Gather yourselves”: should it not say “Gather,” as in “Gather My faithful ones to Me”? Rather, we know that “Gather yourselves” comes from the place above: gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single unity. “I will tell you”—what does “I will tell” mean? It is a mystery of wisdom. Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Shimon: We learned that “I will tell,” “he told,” “they will tell,” and similar forms are a mystery of wisdom. Why does this expression embody a mystery of wisdom? He answered: Because the letters gimel and dalet come together without separation. This is the mystery of wisdom: a word that comes in completeness through the mystery of the letters is such when they are in wisdom. But dalet without gimel is not complete, nor is gimel without dalet. They are bound to one another without separation; whoever separates them brings death upon himself, and this is the mystery of Adam’s sin. Therefore this expression is a mystery of wisdom. Although a yod sometimes stands between gimel and dalet, it causes no separation: everything is a single bond. Thus the expression is certainly precise. “I will tell you”—a mystery of wisdom: he wished to reveal the final outcome of all Israel’s deeds.”

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4: “Rabbi Yehudah says: When Israel heard “I am Hashem your God,” Torah study was fixed in their hearts; they would learn and not forget. : “Everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it is written, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,” and there it is written, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as there it means the very day on which he was speaking, so here it means the very day.”

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז ב) בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 47b: ““God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. “His work that He had done,” not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that issues from Wisdom. “The seventh day” appears here three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day”—three times. “God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, for through this seventh day the world was perfected, as we have said.”
